diagnostic.title: Map your practice path
diagnostic.intro: Ten self-reported questions produce an operating route, missing-evidence list, and next three actions. This is business education, not a legal, tax, clinical, licensing, payer, privacy, or compliance determination.

questions.legend: What would a different work structure need to change for you?

options.label: More choice about clients or services
More control over schedule or workload
Build an asset, team, or broader business
I am still defining the change

questions.legend: Which statement best describes your current professional position?

options.label: Independent authority or license is still pending

questions.legend: When might you want a new structure operating?
How much protected nonclinical launch time can you use each week for the next 90 days?

options.label: I have not protected the time

questions.legend: Which client-payment model are you considering?
How visible are your practice economics today?

options.label: I can state target sessions, realized rate, fixed costs, nonclinical hours, and runway
I have not started the numbers

questions.legend: What evidence do you have that appropriate clients can find or be referred to you?
How much routine business administration do you want to own personally?

options.label: I am comfortable owning most of it
I will own selected work and delegate the rest
I want most of it coordinated or delegated

questions.legend: Which complexity level best describes the launch you are considering?

options.label: One state, solo, no employees or partners
Insurance panels or credentialing are central
More than one state, employees, partners, group practice, public payers, or a lease

questions.legend: Which route do you most want to investigate now?

options.label: Validate while keeping my current work
Build a hybrid or payer-supported practice
Join or contract with a supported platform or group
Buy an existing practice or business
Separately compare franchise or other structured ownership

clarify.title: Clarify Before Spending
clarify.summary: Your answers point to missing operating evidence that should be resolved before major filing, software, or launch commitments.
clarify.tradeoff: Speed now versus preserving the ability to change the model cheaply.
nextActions: Write the three outcomes the practice must produce
Complete the capacity and economics worksheet
Identify the first official or professional question that could change the route
clarify.nonConclusions: This result does not determine professional eligibility, financial suitability, or whether you should open a practice.

lean.title: Lean Solo Validation
lean.summary: Your answers support investigating a focused one-state solo operating model with minimal fixed commitments and a deliberate demand test.
lean.tradeoff: More direct control versus personally owning more acquisition and operating work.
nextActions: Model sessions, realized rate, nonclinical hours, and runway
Get the regulated entity and tax questions answered by the appropriate professionals
Choose one measurable referral or search demand test
lean.nonConclusions: This result does not select cash pay, an entity, a filing state, a tax election, or a clinical model.

hybrid.title: Hybrid and Payer Operations
hybrid.summary: Your answers make credentialing, billing, documentation, reimbursement timing, and payer administration central operating dependencies.
hybrid.tradeoff: Potential payer-sourced volume and access versus additional administrative and reimbursement constraints.
nextActions: Map payer, credentialing, billing, and cash-flow dependencies
Assign each regulated or payer question to a qualified owner
Compare a self-managed stack with specialist or platform-supported fulfillment
hybrid.nonConclusions: This result does not recommend a payer, interpret a contract, determine credentialing eligibility, or establish billing compliance.

supported.title: Supported Path Comparison
supported.summary: Your answers support comparing models that provide more infrastructure, coordination, or an existing operating system before committing to a standalone build.
supported.tradeoff: More support and structure versus fees, constraints, and reduced operating independence.
nextActions: Define the support you require and the control you will not trade away
Compare join, contract, buy, and independent-build paths against the same criteria
Request a separate franchise comparison only if that vehicle is genuinely relevant
supported.nonConclusions: This result does not recommend a transaction, platform, practice, franchise, or ownership structure.
